name: Saint John Vianney
history: A farmer’s son who struggled with his studies and was nearly refused ordination, John Vianney was sent in 1818 to Ars, a small village near Lyon where faith had grown cold. By prayer, penance and long hours in the confessional he transformed it, and pilgrims came from all over France to confess to him. He is the patron of parish priests.
life: Jean-Marie Vianney grew up in the years of the Revolution, when Mass was said in secret, and made his First Communion behind shuttered windows. He began his studies late and found Latin almost impossible; the patient Abbé Balley tutored him, and he was ordained in 1815. In 1818 he became curé of Ars, a village of a little over two hundred people. He visited every family, catechised the children, preached against drunkenness and Sunday work, and spent hours before the tabernacle. In time he heard confessions for eleven hours a day and more, and by his later years some twenty thousand pilgrims a year came to Ars. Several times he tried to slip away to a life of solitude, and each time he returned. He lived on very little and gave away everything he had. He died in 1859, was canonised in 1925 and named patron of parish priests in 1929.
prayerTo: Saint John Vianney, you gave your life to the souls of one small parish and to all who came to you for mercy. Pray for my parish priest and for all priests, that they may be holy, and for me, that I may make a good confession and return to God with my whole heart. Amen.
penance: Pray for your parish priest by name today, and if you can, do something practical for him or for your parish.
meditation: An old peasant told the curé what he did during his long visits in church: I look at Him and He looks at me. Sit before Christ for five minutes today and let yourself be looked at.
